Liam (acme-inc): Hey team — seeing a weird stream behavior from the Python SDK. We start a streaming completion, connection drops mid-token, we reconnect with the same request-id and get a mix of duplicated and missing tokens. Output ends up truncated and then a rerun gives the same partial output. Billing double-charged for the resumed attempt too.
Jana (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro? Which SDK and versions? Exact logs if possible.
Liam (acme-inc): Using python-client v0.9.4. Minimal flow: 1) open SSE to /v1/streams with idempotency header X-Req-Id; 2) after 12 tokens, TCP reset; 3) client reconnects immediately with last-event-id header set to last event id; 4) server replies with some buffered frames then jumps ahead skipping a chunk (so tokens 13-15 missing), then duplicate token 16 appears twice. Logs: 
```
RECV: event:data id=evt-00012 payload="...token12"
CONN: reset by peer
SEND: GET /v1/streams... Last-Event-Id: evt-00012 X-Req-Id: req-abc-123
RESP: 200 OK
RECV: event:data id=evt-00013 payload="...token13"
RECV: event:data id=evt-00016 payload="...token16"
RECV: event:data id=evt-00016 payload="...token16"
RECV: event:data id=evt-00018 payload="...token18"
```
Billing shows two partial usages counted.
Jana (support): Thanks — that helps. Noted SDK + headers. Is this reproducible on node/ts SDK too?
Liam (acme-inc): Only tried Python so far. Node client behaved differently in older run (it would just reconnect and stream continued). We rolled python update recently.
Tori (eng-runtime): Pinged. This smells like a resume-handling race where the server's event sequencing and the runtime's KV-cache mapping diverge after a rapid reconnect. Are you using reserved-dedicated or hosted?
Liam (acme-inc): Hosted. Region us-west-2.
Tori (eng-runtime): Ok. Preliminary hypothesis: when a reconnect happens quickly, two sources can write to the same stream shard — the prior connection's in-flight buffer gets flushed asynchronously and server-side reorder logic uses a 16-bit per-request sequence counter that can overflow/skip when we reconcile resumed checkpoints. That could explain missing frames (we drop if seq <= last_applied) and duplicates (replay of buffered frames).
Nate (eng-ml): Adding that the Python SDK recently changed iterator semantics to eagerly ack events to the application as they arrive (to unblock await), whereas Node kept a small reorder buffer. If server resumes earlier than buffer, client ack state may mismatch causing drop.
Liam (acme-inc): So is this a server bug or SDK regression?
Jana (support): We're triaging both. Any quick mitigation for customers?
Tori (eng-runtime): Immediate workaround: recommend clients set a short resume-backoff (200-400ms) before reconnecting so server's flush completes. Also set X-Stream-Checkpoint header to include the final byte-offset (we'll start returning it in canary) — that gives an absolute resume anchor instead of seq counters.
Nate (eng-ml): For billing double-charge: we need to ensure resumed requests reuse the same billing token id. As a short-term fix, advise customers to not reuse the same idempotency request header when they intend a resumed continuation; instead treat reconnect as the same session and use Last-Event-Id only (no new request-id). We're investigating charging path.
Liam (acme-inc): Not ideal for us — we relied on X-Req-Id to retry safely.
Tori (eng-runtime): Understood. Longer-term fix: we've got a patch that 1) switches the resume protocol to a monotonic 64-bit checkpoint on the server and 2) has SDKs implement a small reorder buffer and de-dup by checkpoint. That should prevent both skips and duplicates. We're preparing a canary release.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: runtime-v1.14.3-canary -> 10% us-west-2 (2027-03-12T14:12:00Z) :rocket:
Jana (support): ETA for SDK patch?
Tori (eng-runtime): We'll land server side change in the next 24 hrs. SDK patches: python-client will add a 64-frame reorder buffer + resume-checkpoint handling in v0.9.5 (canary tomorrow), TS/Node in v1.3.2.
Nate (eng-ml): Tests to run: reproduce with immediate reconnect (0ms), short backoff (250ms) and long backoff (2s); verify no token gaps and single billing event. Also fuzz 1-3 concurrent reconnects.
Liam (acme-inc): Thanks. Can you add me to canary? I can help validate.
Jana (support): Adding Liam to canary group and opening internal ticket with priority P1 for billing.
Jana (support): Action items: 1) eng-runtime: finish canary patch + expose X-Stream-Checkpoint (Tori) 2) SDKs: implement reorder/de-dup using checkpoint (Nate) 3) Billing: audit double-counting for resumed sessions (Finance ops) 4) Support: notify affected customers and recommend 250ms reconnect backoff until patch (Jana).
Tori (eng-runtime): I'll post a short note here when canary metrics look clean. For now, please do not rotate API keys for reproductions.
Liam (acme-inc): Confirmed I got canary invite, will test with our python flow tonight and report. Thanks all. :pray:
